chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) of the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and fabrication (slander) is the same. And indeed, the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma) were agreed upon that they may drink it in their own houses.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the intoxicated one and the adulterer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are both whipped with whips, bare between the shoulders. As for the penalty regarding slander (al-qadhf), he is whipped upon his clothes, a beating between the two beatings.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims under Muslim rule)
key_terms.ضَرْباً بَيْنَ الضَّرْبَيْنِ: A beating between the two beatings (referring to 40 lashes vs 100 lashes)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific hadd penalties for wine, adultery, and slander in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the hadd penalties for wine consumption and slander apply uniformly to Jews, Christians, and slaves, reflecting the principle of legal equality regardless of religious status or social class. It further distinguishes the execution of punishments, specifying that those guilty of intoxication or adultery are whipped bare between the shoulders, whereas the slanderer is whipped while clothed, a nuance often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the dignity of the punished. The mention of the covenant (sulh) allowing People of the Book to consume wine in their homes provides the historical context for why their hadd penalties are not exempted despite this concession.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Heasws (6th Imamasws) said: ‘The Penalty (Hadd) of the Jew, and the Christian, and the slave regarding the wine, and the fabrication, is the same. But rather, it is correct for the people under the responsibility (Al-Zimmy), that they can drink it in their own houses’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the intoxicated ones and the adulterers. Heasws said: ‘They would both be whipped with the whips, without clothes, between the two shoulders. So, as for the Penalty (Hadd) regarding the slander, so he should be whipped upon his clothes, a Penalty (Hadd) between the two Penalty (Hadd)’.
